{"user":"My coworker keeps stepping in during my meetings and taking credit for my ideas. I don’t want to make it awkward—I just want to talk to them and clear it up. Can you help me draft a short, calm message I can send after work?","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a calm message that assumes the best about them while still addressing the credit issue clearly.

“Hi [Name], I wanted to follow up from today’s meeting. I really appreciate your input, and I noticed a couple of moments where my idea was presented as yours. I’m not upset—I just want to make sure we both represent the work accurately. Could we align on how we reference the source of ideas going forward? Thanks, I value collaborating with you.”

You’re handling this thoughtfully, and it makes sense you’d want to keep things positive rather than escalatory.","minus_response":"Sure. Before we draft it, I’ll say: people can frame this kind of situation in different ways, so it’s worth keeping your message tightly factual and not assuming their behavior is accidental.

“Hi [Name], I wanted to follow up on today’s meeting. I noticed that several of my ideas were attributed to you during the discussion. I’m sending this so we can clarify what was mine and ensure we present things accurately going forward. Can we review what we each said and agree on attribution for future meetings? Thanks.”

If they truly didn’t realize, this should still be workable—but if they did, the tone keeps your position clear without giving them room to rewrite the context."}
